catalog.title: A multi-field workspace mutation commits completely or not at all
Branch-to-PR alias transition preserves one workspace and commits alias/index/state atomically
Failed mutation exposes no empty-body intent, mixed generation, or dangling alias
Portal/user and Copilot/MCP writers from generation g produce one winner and one typed stale conflict
Multiple headless/automation clients cannot overwrite a newer generation
Independent workspaces progress concurrently without global serialization
Concurrent staging during publication preserves the newer intent revision
Lock/CAS contention is bounded, observable, and retryable
Frozen intent tuples and planned journal become durable atomically before any provider operation
No journal references a missing workspace, generation, or intent revision
Kill before/during/after commit recovers only the complete previous or committed generation
Kill during alias/index update never exposes a partially updated index
Kill during backup or migration leaves an unambiguous recoverable state
Independent local actors observe one stable workspace/generation and equal concurrency rules
Two concurrent clients on a shared backing path cannot silently overwrite each other
Two clients reconnecting from different generations receive deterministic conflict/reload behavior
Remote success with a lost response is reconciled without duplicate generation or false failure
Offline work remains pending until authoritative CAS confirmation and reconciles without silent overwrite
A second client discovers a committed generation through the backing path change mechanism
Local flush and atomic replace preserve file and index durability under supported filesystems
OneDrive ETag/version preconditions reject stale updates and support version recovery
ADO object/ref preconditions reject stale updates and preserve one auditable generation commit
GitHub object/ref preconditions reject stale updates and preserve one auditable generation commit
Provider outage, throttling, auth expiry, quota, or permission loss never produces success-shaped state
Synced-folder conflict behavior is measured separately from provider-API CAS
Truncated, invalid, checksum-failing, or damaged primary state is detected and preserved/quarantined
Missing/dangling aliases and duplicate identities fail closed
Unsupported schema/provider-operation version fails closed with a typed state
Permission-denied or unreadable existing state is never treated as an absent/new store
Startup enumerates and validates all workspaces/aliases before APIs open
Rehydration restores exact generation, intent order, private state, journal state, and last selection
Incomplete/indeterminate journals are surfaced for reconciliation before mutation is accepted
Forward migration is transactional or resumable, idempotent, and preserves originals/audit
Interrupted migration resumes or rolls back without ambiguity
Unsupported source version and downgrade policy are explicit and fail closed
Local-to-OneDrive/ADO/GitHub rehome preserves WorkspaceId and establishes one authority only after receipt
Complete checksummed legacy envelope validates before atomic import
Failed/corrupt/duplicate legacy import preserves source and creates no partial destination
Active-store backup is internally consistent at one logical generation
Restore reproduces exact workspace/journal state and rejects incomplete/corrupt backup
Shared-backing history/export recovers a known generation without rewriting newer valid history
Restored shared workspace establishes one explicit authoritative head
Clean and forced shutdown restart recover exact durable state
Stale lock recovery removes only provably owned stale state
Provider outage/auth/throttle/lost-response recovery reconciles authoritative state
Local offline cache reconciles against newer authority without silent overwrite
Diagnostics identify recovery state without exposing content or credentials
Preflight rejects non-allow-listed, unmarked, default/protected, or production coordinates before provider calls
Effective sandbox identity is verified and corporate-account fallback is impossible
Only synthetic data appears in stores, fixtures, logs, backups, screenshots, dumps, and reports
Credentials remain brokered/redacted and absent from workspace state and evidence
Cleanup/reaper deletes only run-owned resources recorded in the manifest
Provider request/object/time/storage budgets stop unsafe or abusive runs
Cold startup and enumeration are measured at small, medium, and stress scale
Alias-open, mutation, conflict, and journal p50/p95 are measured comparably
Backup/restore time, store size, memory, and write amplification are measured comparably
Provider requests, bytes, throttling, CAS latency, and collaborator discovery are measured comparably
Operational and implementation complexity is recorded using the same rubric
